  This manuscript is a reusable starting point for evidence-based scientific articles authored with Quarto and rendered with an SBC-compatible LaTeX layout. Replace this text with a concise statement of context, objective, method, principal results, and conclusions.

  Este manuscrito é um ponto de partida reutilizável para artigos científicos baseados em evidências, escritos com Quarto e renderizados com layout LaTeX compatível com a SBC. Substitua este texto por uma síntese do contexto, objetivo, método, principais resultados e conclusões.

# Introduction

State the scientific context, research problem, gap, objective, research questions, and contributions. Every substantive claim should be supported by evidence or an appropriate citation. The bibliography integration is exercised with a real reference from the supplied SBC example [@knuth:84].

# Background and Related Work

Position the contribution against verifiable peer-reviewed literature. Do not fabricate references; use explicit citation placeholders when evidence still needs to be collected.

# Methodology

Describe the problem formulation, data, algorithms, models, baselines, preprocessing, and implementation choices with explicit provenance to the research repository.

# Experimental Design

Document research questions or hypotheses, datasets or benchmark instances, factors, metrics, software and hardware environment, randomization, seeds, statistical procedures, and reproducibility constraints.

# Results

Report only results traceable to machine-readable experiment outputs. Prefer programmatically generated tables and figures to manually transcribed values.

# Discussion

Separate empirical observations from interpretation. Discuss scientific and practical implications without generalizing beyond the experimental evidence.

# Threats to Validity

Discuss construct, internal, external, and conclusion validity when relevant to the research design.

# Reproducibility

Explain how the repository, datasets, environments, experiment scripts, frozen outputs, and manuscript rendering relate to one another. Expensive experiments should normally run outside the GitHub Pages workflow; their saved outputs can be consumed by the manuscript.

# Conclusion

Summarize the supported findings, limitations, and well-grounded directions for future research.
